title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: R package providing fast estimation, simulation, model selection routines discrete-time Dynamic Stochastic Block Models (DSBM). package features accelerated Classification Expectation-Maximization (CEM) algorithm, asymmetric M-step, high-performance C++ subroutines powered Rcpp Armadillo, innovative Perturbed SVD Multi-Start Initialization Strategy. Developed part Master’s Thesis Statistics Gianfilippo Tito, extending hybrid estimation methodology Marino & Pandolfi (2022) dynamic temporal graph architectures.

title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: Dynamic Stochastic Block Models extend static stochastic block models temporal graph structures, allowing latent block memberships nodes transition across discrete time snapshots t=1,…,Tt = 1, \dots, T governed first-order Markov chain. Let 𝐘∈{0,1}n×n×T\mathbf{Y} \\{0, 1\}^{n \times n \times T} denote binary temporal adjacency tensor observed nn vertices across TT discrete observation horizons. Let Ui,t∈{1,…,k}U_{, t} \\{1, \dots, k\} latent community membership node ii time tt. model parameters parameterised 𝛉=(𝛑0,𝚷,𝚿)\boldsymbol{\theta} = (\boldsymbol{\pi}_0, \boldsymbol{\Pi}, \boldsymbol{\Psi}): Initial class proportions: 𝛑0∈Δk−1\boldsymbol{\pi}_0 \\Delta^{k-1}, π0,u=ℙ(Ui,1=u)\pi_{0, u} = \mathbb{P}(U_{, 1} = u). First-order Markov transition matrix: 𝚷∈[0,1]k×k\boldsymbol{\Pi} \[0, 1]^{k \times k}, Πu,v=ℙ(Ui,t=v∣Ui,t−1=u)\Pi_{u, v} = \mathbb{P}(U_{, t} = v \mid U_{, t-1} = u) ∑v=1kΠu,v=1\sum_{v=1}^k \Pi_{u, v} = 1. Dyadic connection probability matrix: 𝚿∈[0,1]k×k\boldsymbol{\Psi} \[0, 1]^{k \times k}, Ψu,v=ℙ(Yi,j,t=1∣Ui,t=u,Uj,t=v)\Psi_{u, v} = \mathbb{P}(Y_{, j, t} = 1 \mid U_{, t} = u, U_{j, t} = v).

title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: Due combinatorial explosion latent trajectory paths multi-modal topography complete-data log-likelihood surface, standard local search heuristics frequently get trapped sub-optimal local extrema. hdsbm tackles problem generalizing Hybrid Maximum Likelihood approach developed Marino & Pandolfi (2022) static SBMs dynamic, time-varying paradigm: Hybrid Classification EM: Combining continuous posterior probabilities (E-step) discrete partition adjustments preserve sharp community boundaries. Dynamic Greedy Reallocation Passes: Extending node--node greedy swaps across temporal slices, accelerated via C++ subroutines. Structured Multi-Start: Coupling deterministic spectral graph embeddings (Truncated SVD) controlled stochastic perturbations ensure global likelihood exploration.

title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: Forward-Backward Recursions (E-step): Computes soft responsibilities hidden temporal transitions via numerically stabilized Hidden Markov Model forward-backward routines. Asymmetric M-step: Simultaneously integrates soft continuous responsibilities hard categorical assignments update 𝛑0\boldsymbol{\pi}_0, 𝚷\boldsymbol{\Pi}, 𝚿\boldsymbol{\Psi}. C++ Accelerated Combinatorial Greedy Search: Accelerates dyadic reallocation passes compiled C++ subroutines (src/Core_hyb.cpp) using RcppArmadillo. Dual-Path Decoding: Delivers pointwise greedy classifications (cl) globally optimal Viterbi state trajectories (clv). Integrated Completed Likelihood (ICL): Tailored penalization criterion separating structural connectivity parameters Markov chain dynamic parameters.

title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: package includes ready--use temporal network dataset toy_hdsbm (n=25n = 25 nodes, k=3k = 3 latent classes, T=4T = 4 snapshots):
code: library(hdsbm) library(mclust)  # 1. Load the dataset (available lazily) data(toy_hdsbm)  # 2. Fit the model with 5 perturbed spectral restarts model <- hdsbm_fit(   Y     = toy_hdsbm$Y,   k     = 3,   nrep  = 5,   seed  = 123 )  # 3. Print summary results (S3 method) print(model)  # 4. Evaluate clustering accuracy vs. ground truth ari_greedy  <- adjustedRandIndex(model$best_fit$cl,  toy_hdsbm$U_true) ari_viterbi <- adjustedRandIndex(model$best_fit$clv, toy_hdsbm$U_true)  cat(sprintf("Adjusted Rand Index (Pointwise Greedy): %.4f\n", ari_greedy)) cat(sprintf("Adjusted Rand Index (Global Viterbi):   %.4f\n", ari_viterbi))  # 5. Extract Model Selection Criterion (ICL) icl(model)

what: 2. Simulating and Estimating a Dynamic Network
title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: Generate synthetic dynamic networks test different persistent Markov regimes:
code: library(hdsbm)  # Dimensional parameters n  <- 30     # Nodes k  <- 3      # Communities TT <- 5      # Time windows  # Ground-truth parameters piv0 <- rep(1 / k, k)  # High persistence Markov transition matrix rho <- 0.1 Pi0 <- rho^abs(outer(seq_len(k), seq_len(k), "-")) Pi0 <- sweep(Pi0, 1, rowSums(Pi0), "/")  # Assortative connectivity matrix (high within-group, low between-group) Psi0 <- matrix(0.04, nrow = k, ncol = k) diag(Psi0) <- c(0.35, 0.40, 0.45)  # Simulate dynamic network sim <- draw_sn_dyn(n = n, k = k, TT = TT, piv = piv0, Pi = Pi0, Psi = Psi0)  # Estimate with SVD multi-start fit <- hdsbm_fit(   Y       = sim$Y,   k       = k,   nrep    = 10,   maxit   = 150,   seed    = 42,   verbose = TRUE )  # Access estimated parameters print(fit)  # Compute numeric ICL or inspect penalty decomposition icl(fit) icl(fit, detailed = TRUE)

title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
code: # Fit models for candidate block counts k in 2:4 k_candidates <- 2:4 fits <- lapply(k_candidates, function(k_val) {   hdsbm_fit(toy_hdsbm$Y, k = k_val, nrep = 5, verbose = FALSE) })  # Compare ICL scores (higher is better) scores <- sapply(fits, icl) names(scores) <- paste0("k=", k_candidates) print(scores)  best_k <- k_candidates[which.max(scores)] cat(sprintf("Optimal number of communities selected by ICL: k = %d\n", best_k))

title: Hybrid Dynamic Stochastic Block Models
text: Adjusted Rand Index (ARI): Evaluates partition recovery accuracy ground-truth community trajectories, invariant label switching. Integrated Completed Likelihood (ICL): ICL=ℓc(𝛉̂∣𝐘,𝐔̂)−k(k+1)4log⁡(Tn(n−1)2)−k(k−1)2log⁡(n(T−1))−k−12log⁡(n) \text{ICL} = \ell_c(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \mid \mathbf{Y}, \hat{\mathbf{U}}) - \frac{k(k+1)}{4}\log\left(T \frac{n(n-1)}{2}\right) - \frac{k(k-1)}{2}\log\left(n(T-1)\right) - \frac{k-1}{2}\log(n)  Penalizes connection probabilities, transition matrices, initial distributions separately guarantee consistent model selection.
